description: Solo builder from Wailuku, Maui — home of the 2023 Lahaina fire. I run kahuola.org, a free hazard platform for Hawaiʻi already ingesting VIIRS fire data daily. Stack: Cloudflare Workers, TypeScript, Leaflet. Looking for teammates to own the pitch video and presentation — code is covered.
summary: NASA plans to begin shutting down Terra and Aqua in late 2026 or early 2027, ending the MODIS fire record that began in 2000. VIIRS continues it, but records about six times as many hot spots, so the two records cannot simply be joined. Kahu Ahi ("keeper of the fire" in Hawaiian) corrects VIIRS detections to the MODIS Aqua scale month by month, tests that correction on years the method had not seen, and publishes both the record and its measured error for all 50 US states and DC and for a Vietnam region. Where the correction fails its own test, the site says "not harmonized" instead of showing a number. It matters because fire agencies, researchers and journalists compare today's fire activity with the past 24 years, and that comparison breaks the day MODIS stops unless the two records are put on one scale with a known error.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Kahu Ahi is an open web app and data pipeline that puts NASA's two generations of satellite fire detections on one scale. It reads NASA FIRMS archive data for MODIS (Terra, Aqua) and VIIRS (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20): more than 15 million detections for the United States and 10 million for a Vietnam region. It keeps presumed vegetation fires, leaves out low-confidence detections, and counts them by day, month, 0.1 degree cell and state.

HOW IT WORKS

For each region and each state, the months when MODIS Aqua and VIIRS both observed give a correction for each calendar month: VIIRS detections divided by Aqua detections. Dividing a VIIRS count by that correction puts it on the MODIS Aqua scale. Every year is then predicted from corrections built without that year, and the error is published. A region or state is shown as harmonized only if it passes a fixed rule (error under 50%, and at least 9 of 12 months with enough detections).

WHAT WE MEASURED (error against MODIS Aqua, on years the method had not seen)

- United States, lower 48 states: VIIRS as recorded is off by 563.8%; with one whole-year ratio, 28.2%; with monthly corrections, 10.4%.

- Vietnam region: 524.7%, 16.8%, 12.0%.

- State by state: 37 of 48 states plus DC pass the test. 12 do not, all places where MODIS Aqua recorded few fires, and are shown as "not harmonized".

- Local corrections matter: Texas is off by 19.4% with its own correction and 47.0% with the national one.

- Alaska and Hawaii are not harmonized: Alaska has enough detections in only 6 of 12 months; in Hawaii most detections are volcanic.

- The correction as actually used for recent months (NOAA-20, near-real-time data) is measured separately: 6.3% for the lower 48 states, 26.1% for the Vietnam region.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

NASA plans to begin shutting down Terra and Aqua in late 2026 or early 2027. Fire agencies, researchers and journalists compare today's fire activity with the past 24 years; that comparison breaks the day MODIS stops unless the two records are on one scale with a known error. On the site you can see where and when satellites detected fire by day, month or year and play it through time; select a detection to read its place, the time of the satellite pass, NASA's image of that day and a one-page report; compare states by tested error; switch to a "VIIRS-only record" that shows the record after Aqua is gone; and download every detection behind every number as CSV.

WHAT IS CREATIVE ABOUT IT

The site refuses to show a number it cannot defend. Where the correction fails its own test, it says "not harmonized" and gives the reason, instead of a confident but wrong figure. It also shows the baselines a simpler method would give, so the reader can see what the monthly correction adds.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

A detection is not a count of fires or burned area. Times are satellite passes, not ignition times, and positions are pixel centres (about 1 km for MODIS, 375 m for VIIRS). Daily corrected values are indicative only, because the correction was tested by month. Recent months use near-real-time data and are marked provisional. An independent script, written only from the README's rules and without the project's code, recomputes every count, correction and error from the raw NASA files: zero differences across all regions and states (AUDIT.md). An outside design review and a security review are in the repository (REVIEW.md, SECURITY_REVIEW.md, QA.md).

TOOLS AND USE OF AI

Python (standard library only) for the pipeline; a static page in HTML and JavaScript with Leaflet, hosted on GitHub Pages. No server, no login, no tracking. Code under Apache License 2.0. The team chose the challenge, set the requirements and the rules the method must keep, and reviewed every result. An AI assistant (Claude, by Anthropic) helped plan the approach and was used to write and test code, draft documentation and draw the Kahu Ahi mark. The demo video's narration is an AI-generated voice (Google Gemini); its picture is a screen recording of the live site. Details: AI_USE.md in the repository.

Live site: https://nguyenhuulong2222.github.io/kahu-ahi/

Code and documentation: https://github.com/nguyenhuulong2222/kahu-ahi

Team Kahu Ahi, Maui, Hawaii (Honolulu Local Event): Long Nguyen, Tiffanie Nguyen, Quynh Thi Kim Do.
